notes: Public APIs and real SplitEdge component/point clicks in a newly owned private Xvfb Rhino session. No user desktop or existing Rhino session was used.
Portable requests substitute the source box recipe for the verified shared artifact. The complete response is JSON-compacted without numerical normalization or array reordering.

The preliminary run exited 2 at polyline-one-shot: the generator supplied points instead of vertices. It produced an error message, not a valid response. The circle was also missing x_axis. Both fixture fields were corrected before the fresh successful 16-case run; no preliminary partial observations are treated as evidence.

An intermediate successful run exposed an ambiguous End test: integer rounding made its Near target the endpoint too. The End aim was moved along the line; the Quad aim was also moved farther along the circle to distinguish coordinates clearly. Only the subsequent fresh complete 16-case run is retained. The independent reference tests require each of these discrete targets to be distinct from and farther from the cursor than Near.
Six families compare one-shot Near with persistent Near-only. Four mixed-mode cases cover End, Mid, Center and Quad competition on a single source curve.

Analytic reference math reads only input source geometry and recorded camera/click, never declared target hypotheses or output geometry. Perspective line fraction conversion is closed-form; circle/quadratic references bracket analytic squared-distance stationary points.

All 16 observed constrained x coordinates agree with their independently computed reference targets within absolute 1e-9. The quadratic ellipse cases have approximately 9.491e-10 residual. This is not zero error or a universal accuracy guarantee.

SplitEdge constrains the target onto the box's x-axis edge, so these observations establish only its x coordinate, not unconstrained 3D snapping parity. Full histories are retained and checked for integrity, not replayed by the native engine.

Near is not yet implemented in the native UI or Rust snap adapter. The fixture is a Rhino-only calibration corpus; generic native replay is not supported yet. Priority beyond the four measured single-object cases and unrestricted curved closest-point solving remain open.
